patch.objective: Replacing stored credentials with system- or user-assigned managed identities

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Study guide for Exam SC-500: Implementing End-to-End Security Controls for Cloud and AI Workloads (page last updated 2026-05-13): identity, access and governance 20-25%, storage, databases and networking 25-30%, compute 20-25%, security posture 20-25%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Bullets quoted: 'Configure Azure private endpoints to secure access to Azure platform as a service (PaaS) resources'; 'Implement and configure Azure Firewall'; 'Implement and configure security controls by using Azure Policy, including built-in and custom policy definitions'; 'Implement and configure managed identities for Azure resources'. The objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: identities must 'be created as Microsoft Entra principals in the database(s) they need to access'; Azure RBAC roles such as SQL DB Contributor 'are used to secure management-related deployment operations, not database connectivity access'; a contained database user is 'CREATE USER [MSEntraUser] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER'; managed identity authentication is token-based and 'preferable since authentication is passwordless'; creating a user for a managed identity needs Microsoft Graph read (Application.Read.All). The page does not mention error 18456 or '<token-identified principal>'; that wording is an authored rendering.
